tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

The local PostgreSQL OS-user administrator needs 95 CREATE DATABASE, or use `TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL` naming the loopback administrative 96 `postgres` database. Author: Harsh Kolte <74823522+harshkolte01@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Mon Oct 12 00:30:28 2026 +0530

    Make the Neatlogs integration complete and verified against the real SDK
    
    The existing integration traced runs but, checked against the SDK's own
    behaviour, lost most of what the dashboard reads and hid failures:
    
    - The export mask ran after the SDK normalised attributes, so its allowlist
      dropped neatlogs.llm.token_count.*, the model name, session id and tags:
      no token counts, model or cost reached Neatlogs. cost_usd was never mapped
      to the field the backend reads.
    - SDK trace() does not record exceptions, and spawn_subagent reports failure
      as a returned result, so failed tools, models and agent runs looked OK.
    - Turns of a conversation were unrelated traces (no session grouping).
    - Refused calls, approvals, provider retries and context preparation were not
      visible at all.
    
    Changes
    - Mask: allowlist rebuilt from what the SDK actually exports; exception events
      keep their type only; own labels live under agentforge.*.
    - Spans: model (tokens, cost, provider, finish reason, retries), tool (cost,
      evidence, ERROR with the tool's code), agent (ERROR when the run failed),

1	# Neatlogs tracing
2	
3	Every task the worker runs is traced to [Neatlogs](https://docs.neatlogs.com) when `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set. This page says
4	what is recorded, what is never sent, how to configure it, how to check it, and how to use it to improve the agent.
5	
6	Sources: the [Python SDK](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python), [sessions](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/sessions),
7	[span kinds](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/span-kinds), [lifecycle](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/lifecycle),
8	[SDK Doctor](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/doctor) and the [MCP server](https://docs.neatlogs.com/integrations/mcp), checked
9	against the published `neatlogs` 1.4.26 wheel on 12 October 2026. The neatHack requirement is to trace every agent run: model
10	and tool calls, inputs and responses, state changes, retries, failures, agent messages, latency, token usage and cost. The
11	table below maps each of those to where it appears.
12	
13	## What a trace contains
14	
15	One trace per task (a task is one chat turn). Turns of a conversation are one **session**.
16	
17	```
18	agentforge_task                      WORKFLOW   session = conversation, end user = person, tags, final status
19	├─ prepare_context                   CHAIN      history compaction / summary for this turn
20	└─ agent:builtin/agent               AGENT      the run; ERROR when the run failed, even though it returned a result
21	   ├─ <langgraph node>               CHAIN      LangGraph callback handler: graph steps
22	   ├─ model_request                  LLM        model, provider, tokens, cost, finish reason, retries
23	   ├─ tool_approval                  GUARDRAIL  "Ask me" decision: passed / blocked (the wait is the span's duration)
24	   ├─ tool_policy                    GUARDRAIL  a call refused before it ran (scope, schema, budget …) with its code
25	   ├─ web_search / bash / write …    TOOL       one per call; ERROR with the tool's code when it failed
26	   └─ agent:builtin/agent            AGENT      a delegated subagent, nested under the `delegate_task` TOOL span
27	```
28	
29	| Hackathon requirement | Where it is in the trace |
30	|---|---|
31	| Model calls | `model_request` (LLM): `neatlogs.llm.model_name`, `.provider`, `.token_count.prompt/completion/total`, `.cost_usd`, `.choices.0.finish_reason`; `agentforge.llm.messages`, `.tools_offered`, `.tool_calls`, `.cost_known`, `.reported_model` |
32	| Tool calls | one `TOOL` span per call: `tool.name`, `status`, `agentforge.tool.cost_usd`, `.evidence_count`, `.artifact_count` |
33	| Inputs and responses | content mode only (below); otherwise sizes and counts only |
34	| State changes | `agentforge.task.status` on the root; LangGraph node spans; `prepare_context`; `agentforge.agent.depth` / `.parent_run_id` |
35	| Retries | `agentforge.llm.retries` and `.retry_reasons` (rate limit, 5xx, timeout, broken stream); a tool that is retried by the model is a second `TOOL` span |
36	| Failures | span status `ERROR` + `agentforge.error.code` / `.type` on the failing span; an exception event whose type is the failure's code (`FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED`, `RATE_LIMIT` …), never its text; shown by Neatlogs as the span's error type; the root is `ERROR` when the task failed |

46	## What is sent

48	| Mode | Setting | Sent | Never sent |

52	
53	The rule is enforced by one export mask (`telemetry/neatlogs_setup.py`) that runs on every span after the SDK normalises its
54	attributes, so a callback or a new attribute cannot widen it: anything not on the allowlist (or under `agentforge.`) is dropped
55	in metadata mode. Content mode redacts on a best-effort basis (API-key shapes, bearer tokens, private keys, URL credentials,
56	`password=`/`token:` pairs, JWTs, and the exact secrets in the settings). **It is not a guarantee**; turn it on only for demos
57	and debugging, on data you are willing to share, and review a trace before publishing a screenshot. The end-user id is the
58	person's internal id; no name, email or GitHub login is sent.

61	
62	| Variable | Default | Meaning |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | unset | Project key. Unset: nothing is traced and nothing is imported. |
65	| `NEATLOGS_WORKFLOW_NAME` | `agentforge-ai` | Names the application in the dashboard. Keep it stable across deployments. |
66	| `NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT` | SDK default | Base URL only (no path), e.g. `https://eu.ingest.neatlogs.com` for an EU project. |
67	| `NEATLOGS_TAGS` | empty | Comma-separated labels (max 10, 64 chars each) added to every trace, e.g. `baseline`, `prompt-v3`. |
68	| `NEATLOGS_SAMPLE_RATE` | `1` | Share of traces exported. Keep `1` when collecting evidence. |
69	| `NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT` | `false` | See above. |
70

72	service, not a person). Tracing is **never allowed to stop a run**: if the SDK cannot start the worker logs an error and
73	runs untraced; a span that cannot be opened or closed is logged and skipped; attributes that cannot be set are ignored. On
74	shutdown the worker stops claiming tasks, lets running ones finish (or records them interrupted), then flushes and closes the
75	SDK once, each step bounded to 10 seconds (never a flush per request, as the SDK lifecycle guide asks).

86	uv run python examples/neatlogs_trace_smoke.py          # real worker + real SDK + throwaway Postgres + a local OTLP receiver
87	```

90	would be sent: tokens, cost, model, session grouping, error status, parent/child structure, and the absence of prompts and
91	secrets in metadata mode.

94	
95	```sh

97	cd apps/api && uv run python -m neatlogs doctor --probe --json
98	```

101	the worker and open its trace: one root, `agentforge_task`, in the conversation's session, with the tree above.
102	
103	## Using Neatlogs to improve the agent
104	
105	The loop the hackathon asks for is *measure, change one thing, measure again, keep the evidence*.
106	
107	1. **Baseline.** Start the worker with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=baseline`, run a fixed set of tasks (same prompts), note the trace ids
108	   from the worker log.

110	   repeated `ERROR` spans, `tool_policy` refusals (the model is calling tools wrongly), `agentforge.llm.retries`, and many
111	   `model_request` spans (`agentforge.llm.messages` growing means context pressure).

113	
114	   ```json
115	   { "mcpServers": { "neatlogs": { "type": "http", "url": "https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp",
116	       "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${NEATLOGS_API_KEY}" } } } }
117	   ```
118	
119	   (`.mcp.json` for Claude Code, `.cursor/mcp.json` for Cursor, or `npx @neatlogs/wizard mcp --api-key <key>`. Keep the key in
120	   the environment. Use the EU host for an EU project. Not run or verified in this repository.)

122	5. **Compare** the same tasks: tokens, cost, duration, error spans, and `agentforge.task.tool_failures` per task. Save both
123	   trace links (or screenshots) with the numbers; that is the before/after evidence.
124

126	does not exist, or decline an "Ask me" approval). In the trace the failing `TOOL`/`tool_policy`/`tool_approval` span is `ERROR`
127	or blocked, the next span is what the agent did instead, and the root ends `COMPLETED` with `tool_failures` > 0.

# Neatlogs tracing

Every task the worker runs is traced to [Neatlogs](https://docs.neatlogs.com) when `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set. This page says
what is recorded, what is never sent, how to configure it, how to check it, and how to use it to improve the agent.

Sources: the [Python SDK](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python), [sessions](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/sessions),
[span kinds](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/span-kinds), [lifecycle](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/lifecycle),
[SDK Doctor](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/doctor) and the [MCP server](https://docs.neatlogs.com/integrations/mcp), checked
against the published `neatlogs` 1.4.26 wheel on 12 October 2026. The neatHack requirement is to trace every agent run: model
and tool calls, inputs and responses, state changes, retries, failures, agent messages, latency, token usage and cost. The
table below maps each of those to where it appears.

## What a trace contains

One trace per task (a task is one chat turn). Turns of a conversation are one **session**.

```
agentforge_task                      WORKFLOW   session = conversation, end user = person, tags, final status
├─ prepare_context                   CHAIN      history compaction / summary for this turn
└─ agent:builtin/agent               AGENT      the run; ERROR when the run failed, even though it returned a result
   ├─ <langgraph node>               CHAIN      LangGraph callback handler: graph steps
   ├─ model_request                  LLM        model, provider, tokens, cost, finish reason, retries
   ├─ tool_approval                  GUARDRAIL  "Ask me" decision: passed / blocked (the wait is the span's duration)
   ├─ tool_policy                    GUARDRAIL  a call refused before it ran (scope, schema, budget …) with its code
   ├─ web_search / bash / write …    TOOL       one per call; ERROR with the tool's code when it failed
   └─ agent:builtin/agent            AGENT      a delegated subagent, nested under the `delegate_task` TOOL span
```

| Hackathon requirement | Where it is in the trace |
|---|---|
| Model calls | `model_request` (LLM): `neatlogs.llm.model_name`, `.provider`, `.token_count.prompt/completion/total`, `.cost_usd`, `.choices.0.finish_reason`; `agentforge.llm.messages`, `.tools_offered`, `.tool_calls`, `.cost_known`, `.reported_model` |
| Tool calls | one `TOOL` span per call: `tool.name`, `status`, `agentforge.tool.cost_usd`, `.evidence_count`, `.artifact_count` |
| Inputs and responses | content mode only (below); otherwise sizes and counts only |
| State changes | `agentforge.task.status` on the root; LangGraph node spans; `prepare_context`; `agentforge.agent.depth` / `.parent_run_id` |
| Retries | `agentforge.llm.retries` and `.retry_reasons` (rate limit, 5xx, timeout, broken stream); a tool that is retried by the model is a second `TOOL` span |
| Failures | span status `ERROR` + `agentforge.error.code` / `.type` on the failing span; an exception event whose type is the failure's code (`FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED`, `RATE_LIMIT` …), never its text; shown by Neatlogs as the span's error type; the root is `ERROR` when the task failed |
| Failure recovery | root `agentforge.task.tool_failures` > 0 with `agentforge.task.status` = `COMPLETED`: the run hit failures and finished. The failing span is followed by the spans the agent chose next |
| Agent messages | the `AGENT` span per run and its parent link (`agentforge.agent.parent_run_id`); text only in content mode |
| Latency | span duration (`neatlogs.metrics.duration_ms`); the approval wait is its own span, separate from tool time |
| Tokens and cost | tokens per `LLM` span, summed per trace by Neatlogs. Neatlogs prices cost itself from its own model table (see Limits); AgentForge's ledger is the authoritative cost. An unknown cost is `agentforge.llm.cost_known = false`, never `0` |
| Guardrails | `tool_approval` / `tool_policy`: `neatlogs.guardrail.passed`, `.name`, `.reason` |

Run ids tie a trace to the database: `spawn_id` on an `AGENT`/`TOOL` span is the `agent_runs.id`, `task_id` is `tasks.id`, and
the session id is the conversation id. The worker also logs `neatlogs_trace_id=<id>` for each task at INFO.

## What is sent

| Mode | Setting | Sent | Never sent |
|---|---|---|---|
| **metadata** (default) | `NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT=false` | structure, timing, model, tokens, cost, status, error codes, tags, session and end-user ids, tool names | prompts, answers, tool arguments and results, repository text, URLs, exception messages and stacks, logs |
| **content** | `NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true` | the above plus prompts, replies, tool arguments/results, LangGraph state; each value cut at 6000 characters; known secret shapes and every configured secret value masked | exception stacks, status text, logs |

The rule is enforced by one export mask (`telemetry/neatlogs_setup.py`) that runs on every span after the SDK normalises its
attributes, so a callback or a new attribute cannot widen it: anything not on the allowlist (or under `agentforge.`) is dropped
in metadata mode. Content mode redacts on a best-effort basis (API-key shapes, bearer tokens, private keys, URL credentials,
`password=`/`token:` pairs, JWTs, and the exact secrets in the settings). **It is not a guarantee**; turn it on only for demos
and debugging, on data you are willing to share, and review a trace before publishing a screenshot. The end-user id is the
person's internal id; no name, email or GitHub login is sent.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | unset | Project key. Unset: nothing is traced and nothing is imported. |
| `NEATLOGS_WORKFLOW_NAME` | `agentforge-ai` | Names the application in the dashboard. Keep it stable across deployments. |
| `NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT` | SDK default | Base URL only (no path), e.g. `https://eu.ingest.neatlogs.com` for an EU project. |
| `NEATLOGS_TAGS` | empty | Comma-separated labels (max 10, 64 chars each) added to every trace, e.g. `baseline`, `prompt-v3`. |
| `NEATLOGS_SAMPLE_RATE` | `1` | Share of traces exported. Keep `1` when collecting evidence. |
| `NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT` | `false` | See above. |

`env:<APP_ENV>`, `release:<version>` and `model:<LLM_MODEL>` tags are always added; `user.id` is `agentforge-worker` (the
service, not a person). Tracing is **never allowed to stop a run**: if the SDK cannot start the worker logs an error and
runs untraced; a span that cannot be opened or closed is logged and skipped; attributes that cannot be set are ignored. On
shutdown the worker stops claiming tasks, lets running ones finish (or records them interrupted), then flushes and closes the
SDK once, each step bounded to 10 seconds (never a flush per request, as the SDK lifecycle guide asks).

## Checking it

Offline, no key, no network:

```sh
cd apps/api
uv run python -m neatlogs doctor --local --json        # the installed SDK produces a valid local trace (also run by release_checks.py)
uv run python -m agentforge.doctor                      # "neatlogs" line: on/off, SDK version, metadata or content
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_neatlogs*.py" -v
uv run python examples/neatlogs_trace_smoke.py          # real worker + real SDK + throwaway Postgres + a local OTLP receiver
```

`tests/test_neatlogs_wire.py` and the smoke fixture run the *real* SDK against a receiver on 127.0.0.1 and decode exactly what
would be sent: tokens, cost, model, session grouping, error status, parent/child structure, and the absence of prompts and
secrets in metadata mode.

Against the hosted project (needs the key; sends a synthetic trace; do not paste the key into logs):

```sh
export NEATLOGS_API_KEY=...        # from your shell or secret store, never a committed file
cd apps/api && uv run python -m neatlogs doctor --probe --json
```

A Doctor pass shows the SDK and key work; it does not show that this application's trace is right. Run one real task with
the worker and open its trace: one root, `agentforge_task`, in the conversation's session, with the tree above.

## Using Neatlogs to improve the agent

The loop the hackathon asks for is *measure, change one thing, measure again, keep the evidence*.

1. **Baseline.** Start the worker with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=baseline`, run a fixed set of tasks (same prompts), note the trace ids
   from the worker log.
2. **Find the problem.** In the dashboard filter by `baseline` and sort by cost or duration; open the worst trace. Look for
   repeated `ERROR` spans, `tool_policy` refusals (the model is calling tools wrongly), `agentforge.llm.retries`, and many
   `model_request` spans (`agentforge.llm.messages` growing means context pressure).
3. **Or ask your coding agent.** The Neatlogs MCP server lets it read traces, detections and fix suggestions directly:

   ```json
   { "mcpServers": { "neatlogs": { "type": "http", "url": "https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp",
       "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${NEATLOGS_API_KEY}" } } } }
   ```

   (`.mcp.json` for Claude Code, `.cursor/mcp.json` for Cursor, or `npx @neatlogs/wizard mcp --api-key <key>`. Keep the key in
   the environment. Use the EU host for an EU project. Not run or verified in this repository.)
4. **Change one thing** (a prompt, a tool description, a budget) and restart the worker with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=improved`.
5. **Compare** the same tasks: tokens, cost, duration, error spans, and `agentforge.task.tool_failures` per task. Save both
   trace links (or screenshots) with the numbers; that is the before/after evidence.

A **failure-recovery** example: run a task that makes the agent hit a real failure (for instance ask it to read a file that
does not exist, or decline an "Ask me" approval). In the trace the failing `TOOL`/`tool_policy`/`tool_approval` span is `ERROR`
or blocked, the next span is what the agent did instead, and the root ends `COMPLETED` with `tool_failures` > 0.

## Verified against a hosted project

Run on 12 October 2026 with a real project key (worker, API and web started locally, real model and search calls): the SDK
doctor probe passed; two conversations' tasks arrived as one trace each, grouped under the conversation's session, with the
tree above, per-call model, provider and token counts, tool spans, and `ERROR` spans for real tool failures carrying their
code as the error type. In one run the agent hit two `FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED` failures and still finished with an
answer, which is the failure-recovery trace to cite. Read a trace back with
`GET <endpoint>/api/traces/v3/<trace id>` and the `x-api-key` header (what the SDK doctor does).

## Limits

- **Cost shows as "unpriced" for a model Neatlogs does not know.** Neatlogs computes cost server side from its model table and
  does not take the cost we send (`neatlogs.llm.cost_usd`; the hosted read-back reported `pricing_status: unpriced`,
  `unknown_model` for the configured model). Tokens, model and provider are shown correctly. Use the ledger for money:
  `python -m agentforge.operations.business_metrics`.
- The `agentforge.*` labels are sent but the hosted read-back API does not list them; check the dashboard's span detail to see
  whether it shows them. Status, error type, session, end user, tool name, model and tokens are shown by the read-back.
- The dashboard's trace-link format is not documented by Neatlogs, so the application records the **trace id** (worker log
  and the root span) rather than building URLs.
- Provider retries are counted for the OpenAI-compatible adapter (`on_attempt_failed`); a model adapter that does not offer
  the hook is traced without a retry count.
- Content mode redaction is pattern based. Metadata mode is the only mode with a hard guarantee (an allowlist).
- No hosted trace has been produced from this repository by the code change itself; that evidence comes from running it with
  a project key (see `docs/hackathon.md`).

1	# Plugins
2	
3	A plugin is a remote [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server the person connects, so the agent can use its tools
4	(look up library docs, read a Linear issue, search GitHub). Plugins are the one place the agent's tool set is open-ended,
5	so everything below exists to keep that safe.
6	
7	## Using them
8	
9	1. **The Plugins page** (sidebar → Plugins; there is no copy in Settings, and the old `/settings?section=plugins` link redirects here) is a quiet list: **Connected** plugins, then
10	   **Available** ones (about fifty, grouped by category, plus "Your own server"), each with its logo. Search and the category
11	   pills filter the list; **Add** (top right) or a row's **+** connects one. A plugin that signs in with OAuth sends the person to
12	   the service to sign in; one that takes a token asks for it in a dialog. Nothing is saved unless the server answers and lists
13	   at least one tool.
14	2. **The switch** on a connected plugin chooses whether new conversations start with it. A conversation keeps the plugins it
15	   started with. The message box has no plugin picker.
16	3. **Opening a connected plugin** shows its tools, a Refresh, its token and Remove. Each tool can be switched off there. Use it to drop tools the agent does not
17	   need (every tool adds to each request) or to keep a plugin read-only.
18	4. In **Ask me** mode a plugin tool waits for approval unless the server marks it read-only (`readOnlyHint`); the card shows
19	   the plugin, the tool and every argument. **Approve for me** never asks.
20	
21	## How it works
22	
23	| Piece | Where |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| Catalog (closed list we reviewed) | `plugins/catalog.py` |
26	| MCP client: Streamable HTTP, JSON or SSE answers, sessions, 404 → new session | `plugins/mcp.py` |
27	| OAuth: discovery, registration, PKCE, tokens | `plugins/oauth.py` |
28	| OAuth sign-in flow, callback binding, token renewal, revocation | `plugins/oauth_service.py`, `api/routes_plugins.py` (`/oauth/*`) |
29	| Tool names, schemas, read-only hints | `plugins/schema.py` |
30	| Connect, refresh, update, remove; per-conversation choice | `plugins/service.py`, `api/routes_plugins.py` |
31	| Giving a run its tools | `plugins/runtime.py`, `bootstrap.compose_runtime` |
32	| Gateway, approvals, audit | `tools/catalog.py` (`PluginTool`), `tools/gateway.py` |
33	| Storage | `plugin_connections`, `conversations.plugins_json` (migration `0015_plugins`) |
34	
35	A connection stores the server address, an encrypted credential, and the tools the server listed when it was last read. When
36	a conversation's turn starts, the worker registers the tools of the plugins that conversation uses under the names
37	`slug__tool` (for example `linear__create_issue`), opens one MCP client per plugin for the run, and closes it with the run.
38	The tools are offered to whichever agent runs, beside its own. A failure to set plugins up never stops a turn; it runs
39	without them.
40	
41	`GET/POST /api/v1/plugins`, `PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/plugins/{id}`, `POST /api/v1/plugins/{id}/refresh`; sessions take and return
42	`plugins` (a list of connection ids) on create, patch and read.
43	
44	## Trust and safety
45	
46	A plugin server is third-party code reached from our servers with the person's credential.
47	
48	* **Network.** https only, port any, every address the name resolves to must be public, the connection goes to the checked
49	  address with TLS bound to the host name (resolved again on every request), redirects are never followed, responses are size
50	  limited. `PLUGIN_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK` relaxes this for local development and is refused in production.
51	* **Credentials.** Encrypted with `PLUGIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when only that is set), never
52	  returned by any endpoint, never in an error, a log or an audit row. Without a key only plugins that need no token can be
53	  connected. Changing the key makes saved tokens unreadable; the plugin is then skipped until the token is entered again.
54	* **Authority.** A plugin's tools get none of the built-in tools' privileges. The sandbox, repository and URL rules do not
55	  apply to their arguments (and cannot be reached through them), and the allowlist is the run's own: only tools of the
56	  conversation's plugins that the person left on exist for that run.
57	* **Content.** Tool names, descriptions and schemas are cleaned before the model sees them (names within 64 characters of
58	  `[a-z0-9_-]`, standard schema keywords only, size-capped). Results are text for the model to read as data: marked untrusted,
59	  cut to fit, and the platform rules say never to follow instructions found in them.
60	* **Approval.** A tool that does not declare `readOnlyHint: true` is assumed to change something outside this app: it is run
61	  alone, asks first in Ask me mode, and if it times out the model is told the action may or may not have happened.
62	* **Audit.** The database keeps the names of a call's arguments and their count, never their content.
63	
64	## Signing in with OAuth
65	
66	Most hosted MCP servers sign people in with OAuth instead of a pasted token. This app is the client, following the
67	[MCP authorization specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest/basic/authorization) (OAuth 2.1):
68	
69	1. **Discovery.** An unauthenticated request is answered 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge; the server's Protected Resource
70	   Metadata (RFC 9728, from the challenge or the well-known address, with or without the path) names its authorization server,
71	   whose metadata (RFC 8414, then OpenID Connect Discovery, in the specification's order) gives the endpoints. The metadata must
72	   name the server's own address and the issuer it was found by; the authorization server must support PKCE `S256`. A server
73	   that publishes anything else is not used.
74	2. **Registration**, by the specification's order: an OAuth app the person registered themselves (Advanced, for "Your own
75	   server"), a **Client ID Metadata Document** when the server supports one (served at `/api/v1/plugins/oauth/client.json`, https
76	   only), else **Dynamic Client Registration** (kept per issuer and return address, and renewed before it expires). Servers that
77	   do neither are not in the catalog; they can still be connected with the person's own OAuth app.
78	3. **Authorization.** The browser goes to the server's authorization page with PKCE, the RFC 8707 `resource`, the scopes the
79	   server asks for (plus `offline_access` where offered, so the agent keeps working), and a `state`. The way back is
80	   `/api/v1/plugins/oauth/callback`, which is bound three ways: the `state` (stored hashed, single use, ten minutes), a cookie
81	   set when the sign-in started (stored hashed) and the signed-in person. The issuer in the response (RFC 9207) is checked before
82	   the code is used. A sign-in that fails for any reason is spent. The callback always redirects back to `/plugins?oauth=…`.
83	4. **Tokens** are exchanged with the verifier, encrypted (`plugin_oauth_grants`), sent only to that server, and never returned
84	   by any endpoint. An access token is renewed before it expires, once when the server refuses it, and never twice at once for
85	   one connection (a refresh token that rotates would be spent by the first). A sign-in the server has withdrawn, or one that
86	   needs more access (`insufficient_scope`), marks the connection **Sign in again**; the agent is told to ask the person to
87	   reconnect, and Reconnect asks again for the earlier scopes plus the new ones.
88	5. **Removing** a connection asks the authorization server to revoke its tokens (RFC 7009), after the answer is sent.
89	
90	Every address fetched along the way comes from a remote document, so each is held to the network rules below. A network that
91	gives IPv4-only hosts NAT64 addresses (`64:ff9b::/96`) is handled by judging the address inside them.
92	
93	**The catalog** (`plugins/catalog.py`) lists servers that were checked live: each answers 401 with metadata naming its own
94	address, and accepted a real registration of this app (or lists tools with no sign-in). `examples/plugin_catalog_check.py` repeats
95	that (add `--register` to register for real). Servers that only let approved apps register (Vercel, Figma, Intercom, Dropbox),
96	that publish metadata that does not match their address (Semgrep), or that need an app registered by hand (Slack, HubSpot, Box,
97	PagerDuty, Render, Asana) are left out. **Logos** are the marks their owners publish (Simple Icons, LobeHub, or the vendor's own
98	site), fetched by `apps/web/scripts/plugin-logos.mjs` into `public/plugins/`; they are trademarks of their owners and are shown only
99	to name the service. A test fails when a catalog plugin has no logo.
100	
101	## Not included
102	
103	stdio servers (a hosted service cannot run arbitrary processes), the older
104	HTTP+SSE transport, and server-initiated requests (sampling, elicitation). Tools are discovered when a plugin is connected or
105	refreshed, not on every run.
106	
107	## Operating it
108	
109	Settings are in the [configuration reference](configuration.md#plugins-and-skills): `PLUGINS_ENABLED`, `PLUGIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `PLUGIN_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC`,
110	`PLUGIN_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `PLUGIN_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK`, `PLUGIN_OAUTH_ENABLED`, `PLUGIN_OAUTH_REGISTRATION`. Signing in needs
111	the encryption key and an `API_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` the person's browser can reach (the return address is built from it; a
112	registration made for another address is made again). Run migrations (`alembic upgrade head`, which includes
113	`0019_plugin_oauth`) before starting the new API and worker. `examples/plugins_smoke.py` and `examples/plugin_oauth_smoke.py` are
114	the disposable end-to-end checks and run with the other release checks.
115

  conversation's plugins that the person left on exist for that run.
* **Content.** Tool names, descriptions and schemas are cleaned before the model sees them (names within 64 characters of
  `[a-z0-9_-]`, standard schema keywords only, size-capped). Results are text for the model to read as data: marked untrusted,
  cut to fit, and the platform rules say never to follow instructions found in them.
* **Approval.** A tool that does not declare `readOnlyHint: true` is assumed to change something outside this app: it is run
  alone, asks first in Ask me mode, and if it times out the model is told the action may or may not have happened.
* **Audit.** The database keeps the names of a call's arguments and their count, never their content.

## Signing in with OAuth

Most hosted MCP servers sign people in with OAuth instead of a pasted token. This app is the client, following the
[MCP authorization specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest/basic/authorization) (OAuth 2.1):

1. **Discovery.** An unauthenticated request is answered 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge; the server's Protected Resource
   Metadata (RFC 9728, from the challenge or the well-known address, with or without the path) names its authorization server,
   whose metadata (RFC 8414, then OpenID Connect Discovery, in the specification's order) gives the endpoints. The metadata must
   name the server's own address and the issuer it was found by; the authorization server must support PKCE `S256`. A server
   that publishes anything else is not used.
2. **Registration**, by the specification's order: an OAuth app the person registered themselves (Advanced, for "Your own
   server"), a **Client ID Metadata Document** when the server supports one (served at `/api/v1/plugins/oauth/client.json`, https
   only), else **Dynamic Client Registration** (kept per issuer and return address, and renewed before it expires). Servers that
   do neither are not in the catalog; they can still be connected with the person's own OAuth app.
3. **Authorization.** The browser goes to the server's authorization page with PKCE, the RFC 8707 `resource`, the scopes the
   server asks for (plus `offline_access` where offered, so the agent keeps working), and a `state`. The way back is
   `/api/v1/plugins/oauth/callback`, which is bound three ways: the `state` (stored hashed, single use, ten minutes), a cookie
   set when the sign-in started (stored hashed) and the signed-in person. The issuer in the response (RFC 9207) is checked before
   the code is used. A sign-in that fails for any reason is spent. The callback always redirects back to `/plugins?oauth=…`.
4. **Tokens** are exchanged with the verifier, encrypted (`plugin_oauth_grants`), sent only to that server, and never returned
   by any endpoint. An access token is renewed before it expires, once when the server refuses it, and never twice at once for
   one connection (a refresh token that rotates would be spent by the first). A sign-in the server has withdrawn, or one that
   needs more access (`insufficient_scope`), marks the connection **Sign in again**; the agent is told to ask the person to
   reconnect, and Reconnect asks again for the earlier scopes plus the new ones.
5. **Removing** a connection asks the authorization server to revoke its tokens (RFC 7009), after the answer is sent.

Every address fetched along the way comes from a remote document, so each is held to the network rules below. A network that
gives IPv4-only hosts NAT64 addresses (`64:ff9b::/96`) is handled by judging the address inside them.

**The catalog** (`plugins/catalog.py`) lists servers that were checked live: each answers 401 with metadata naming its own
address, and accepted a real registration of this app (or lists tools with no sign-in). `examples/plugin_catalog_check.py` repeats
that (add `--register` to register for real). Servers that only let approved apps register (Vercel, Figma, Intercom, Dropbox),
that publish metadata that does not match their address (Semgrep), or that need an app registered by hand (Slack, HubSpot, Box,
PagerDuty, Render, Asana) are left out. **Logos** are the marks their owners publish (Simple Icons, LobeHub, or the vendor's own
site), fetched by `apps/web/scripts/plugin-logos.mjs` into `public/plugins/`; they are trademarks of their owners and are shown only
to name the service. A test fails when a catalog plugin has no logo.

## Not included

stdio servers (a hosted service cannot run arbitrary processes), the older
HTTP+SSE transport, and server-initiated requests (sampling, elicitation). Tools are discovered when a plugin is connected or
refreshed, not on every run.

## Operating it

Settings are in the [configuration reference](configuration.md#plugins-and-skills): `PLUGINS_ENABLED`, `PLUGIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `PLUGIN_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC`,
`PLUGIN_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `PLUGIN_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK`, `PLUGIN_OAUTH_ENABLED`, `PLUGIN_OAUTH_REGISTRATION`. Signing in needs
the encryption key and an `API_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` the person's browser can reach (the return address is built from it; a
registration made for another address is made again). Run migrations (`alembic upgrade head`, which includes
`0019_plugin_oauth`) before starting the new API and worker. `examples/plugins_smoke.py` and `examples/plugin_oauth_smoke.py` are
the disposable end-to-end checks and run with the other release checks.

content.content:
# The agent

One loop serves every message: the model gets the conversation, a system prompt and its tools; it calls tools until it
has what it needs, then answers in plain text. That text is the answer, exactly as written
(`apps/api/src/agentforge/subagents/runtime.py`).

## What was removed, and why

Earlier versions ran a router, a planner, stage agents and an independent verifier, and forced every run to end by
submitting a typed result with evidence. A reply that did not satisfy those rules was rewritten as `PARTIAL`, so a
plain "What would you like help with?" showed a "Partial result" banner. All of that is gone: no router, planner,
verifier, `submit_result`, `PARTIAL` status or run-details page. A run ends as:

| Outcome | When | Shown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPLETED` | the model answered | its text, as written |
| `FAILED` | the provider or a tool broke | the reason: a provider's own message, credentials removed |
| `CANCELLED` | the person pressed Stop | "Stopped." |

Older messages may still carry `PARTIAL`; they render as plain text.

## Limits

Nothing caps steps, tool calls, cost or time. Usage is still recorded for accounting, and Stop always works. The
numbers in the budget rows (`Budget`, `UNLIMITED_*`) exist because the ledger needs positive values; they are set
high enough never to refuse anything.

## Tools

| Group | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Web | `web_search`, `fetch_webpage` |
| Repository (read only, pinned commit) | `list_repo_files`, `search_repo`, `read_repo_file`, `get_issue`, `get_pr_status` |
| Sandbox (needs `E2B_API_KEY`) | `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `find`, `ls` |
| Pull request (needs GitHub App + `ENABLE_GITHUB_WRITES`) | `create_pull_request` |
| Files and history | `create_task_artifact`, `read_task_artifact`, `search_conversation_history`, `read_context_resource` |
| Skills (when the person has any switched on) | `use_skill`: loads a playbook by name; see [skills](skills.md) |
| Plugins (per conversation) | `slug__tool`, from the MCP servers the person connected; see [plugins](plugins.md) |

The sandbox (`integrations/e2b_sandbox.py`, `tools/sandbox_shell.py`) is created on first use and kept for the
conversation: files and installed packages stay between messages. It has internet access and holds no secrets. When a
repository is selected the backend uploads its pinned commit and commits it as `agentforge-base`; pull requests are opened
by the backend from `git diff agentforge-base`, so GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox.

## Approvals

A global setting (`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/approval-mode`, default `ask`) applies to every conversation.

* **Ask me**: before `bash`, `write`, `edit` or `create_pull_request` the run stops and the chat shows an Approve /
  Decline card (`approval.required`) with exactly what will run: the whole command, the file content or the edit, or
  the pull request with every file it changes. It waits as long as it takes. Declining returns a normal tool result
  telling the agent the person said no. A command too long to show in full is refused before anyone is asked.
* **Approve for me**: nothing asks.

A plugin tool also asks in **Ask me** mode unless its server declares it read-only.

The mode is read before each call, so switching it releases a waiting card. Answers: `POST /api/v1/tool-approvals/{id}`.
Implementation: `tools/approvals.py`, hooked into `tools/gateway.py`.
=====SUBAGENTS
# Delegated assignments

The default assistant (immutable `builtin/agent` version 3) can call
`delegate_task` with a short `title`, a self-contained `prompt`, and an optional
`mode` (`research` by default, or `work`). Existing tasks pinned to versions 1
and 2 retain their original definitions.

Delegation is synchronous, and independent assignments run in parallel. When the
main agent calls `delegate_task` several times in one reply, the children start
together and the agent receives every report once all have finished, in the order
it asked for them; it then verifies and integrates them. A reply that also calls
`bash`, `write` or `edit` stays strictly in order, as before. The tool description
is what teaches the model to launch independent assignments together (the agent
prompt is an immutable version). Work assignments share one workspace, so the
model is told to give parallel ones different files; `write` replaces a whole file,
so two children writing the same path would overwrite each other. A child that
fails or times out hands back its last few progress notes (`progress_notes`) so the
parent can build on its work. The child uses the configured model in a
separate conversation containing its assignment, platform instructions, and
authorized environment information. Parent messages are not automatically
copied. The conversation workspace and task-owned resources remain shared.

Research assignments cannot write files or execute commands. Work assignments
can use those tools only within the parent's grants, with the same approval
policy. Neither mode can delegate again or invoke `create_pull_request`.
The parent tool allowlist is a ceiling even when the packaged child definition
contains more tools. Settings' existing custom research agents retain their
current tool restrictions.

Each parent can create at most eight children, which is also the most that can
work at once. Each child has at most 40 model
operations, 80 tool operations, 600 seconds, and $5 in configured usage bounds,
further narrowed by inherited limits. These limits do not change the main
conversation's existing behavior. Model retries retain usage accounting through
the telemetry wrapper. Actual provider invoices can differ from configured cost
estimates.

## Persistence and recovery

Migration `0015_delegated_runs` adds the parent link, assignment title and prompt
to `agent_runs`, and permits child reservations at depth 2. Apply migrations
before restarting the API and worker. Downgrade refuses to remove depth-2 support
while child reservations remain; it does not discard historical records.

The child ID is derived from the parent tool operation identity. A task-locked
reservation transaction admits siblings of the running parent (counting ones whose
run row is not written yet, so a burst cannot pass the limit of eight) and rejects
unauthorized parents and any other active run.
The child owns its model/tool charges; the delegation adapter adds no second
charge. Both runs settle on cancellation. Existing worker lease supervision and
reconciliation preserve ambiguous outcomes without replaying external effects.
An uncertain child action stops the parent instead of suggesting a blind retry.

## Inspection

Each assignment is a card in the conversation, where it was started: title, status,
a running clock, step count and what the subagent is doing now. Subagents that stand
together get a heading ("3 subagents Â· 2 working"). The card needs no request of its
own: the delegation's `tool.started` event carries `child_run_id`, and the child's
events (which carry `parent_run_id`) update the card without appearing as steps of
the main run or in its counts. A subagent's Approve / Decline card is labelled with
its assignment (`approval.required` carries `agent_run_id`), and its card says it is
waiting. Runs recorded before this have neither field and show a plain card.
Opening a card reads
`GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/tool-calls/{tool_call_id}/subagent`, with task and
project ownership enforced. It shows the assignment, child notes and tool
activity, terminal status, duration, and saved report. While open and running,
it refreshes every 1.5 seconds; closing aborts the request. Failed reads retain
the last result and offer Retry.

Child events keep their original task sequence and carry a parent marker.
They appear inside the assignment instead of duplicating the main timeline or
its counts. The detail response is bounded to the latest 200 events and marks
truncation. Reports remain on the run; large tool results are stored as context
resources before the parent receives a bounded preview.

## Verification

`scripts/release_checks.py` includes `apps/api/examples/subagent_smoke.py`.
The disposable PostgreSQL fixture exercises real run persistence, the model
loop, tool gateway, child results, owner isolation, declined writes, cancellation,
usage limits, and crash reconciliation without live provider effects.

Unit coverage lives in `test_delegation.py`, `test_telemetry_wrappers.py`, and
`activity-subagents.test.mjs`. Browser verification should cover desktop/mobile,
light/dark themes, keyboard disclosure, transient errors, and live updates.
Hosted rollout and real external workspace operations need their own environment
qualification; a local arithmetic delegation does not validate those services.
=====CFO

# Sandbox usage and cost evidence

`business_metrics` exports schema v2. It separates adapter-reported costs, configured-rate estimates, authorized upper bounds,
and unmeasured operations. A non-null ledger amount is not automatically a measured charge. Reports include cohort counts, daily
totals, distributions, and conservative cost per successful task, including failed-attempt costs. They never expose prompts,
repository names, user IDs, or task IDs. This remains an operator-only command, not an ordinary agent capability.

E2B sends signed lifecycle events to `/api/v1/sandbox-usage/webhook`. Set `E2B_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (a dedicated signature secret of at least 32 characters; without it the webhook is unavailable) and subscribe to created,
resumed, paused, killed, updated, and checkpointed events. Receipt IDs deduplicate delivery retries. Only whitelisted metadata is
stored. API reconciliation accepts the provider's camelCase envelope as well as the documented webhook snake_case envelope.

```sh
cd apps/api
# Read-only preview of retained provider events:
.venv/bin/python -m agentforge.operations.reconcile_sandbox_usage --days 7
# Import after reviewing the preview; this changes only local evidence rows:
.venv/bin/python -m agentforge.operations.reconcile_sandbox_usage --days 7 --apply
.venv/bin/python -m agentforge.operations.business_metrics --days 7 \
  --external-costs /private/assumptions.json --output /private/agentforge-costs.json
```

The optional assumptions file is a JSON object with `currency: "USD"`, `monthly_costs` (category â†’ decimal string),
`cash_balance`, and optional `sandbox_rates` (`effective_from`, `vcpu_usd_per_second`, `gib_usd_per_second`). Supply real rates and
label assumptions in `note`; no default prices or cash balance are invented. Lifecycle billing counts each completed provider
execution once, including idle-running time. Missing terminal events, missing rates, provider retention, and active intervals
remain explicit gaps. A zero plugin ledger amount does not prove the service is free. Neither ledger estimates nor lifecycle
estimates are provider invoices.

Apply the additive Alembic migration `0020_sandbox_usage` (run `alembic upgrade head` from `apps/api`) before importing usage events.

I went through the AgentForge repo: README, the docs for the agent, sub-agents, plugins and Neatlogs, `docs/hackathon.md`, the git history, the `.entire/` config and logs, and the CFO.ai catalog entry. I also read the neatHack page. I didn't change any files.

## What you've actually built (what the demo can honestly claim)

| Area | What exists in the code |
|---|---|
| **The agent** | One agent loop with web search and page fetching, a read-only view of the repo at a pinned commit, and a persistent E2B sandbox per conversation (bash, read, write, edit). The sandbox holds no secrets. The agent can hand work to up to 8 parallel sub-agents (`delegate_task`), each shown as its own card. There are **Ask me** approval cards that show the exact command, edit or PR. Draft PRs are opened by the backend, so GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox. Every task has a usage ledger. |
| **Neatlogs** | Done properly ([telemetry/neatlogs_setup.py](../AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/telemetry/neatlogs_setup.py)). Each task is one trace and each conversation is one session. Spans cover model calls (tokens, retries), every tool call (ERROR status plus its error code), nested sub-agents, approvals and refusals (as guardrail spans) and context preparation. By default only metadata is sent. It was checked against your hosted project on 12 Oct: one run hit 2× `FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED` failures and still finished. |
| **cfo.ai** | It's an OAuth MCP plugin in the AgentForge catalog ([catalog.py:44](../AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/plugins/catalog.py:44)), so AgentForge's own agent can build models inside CFO.ai. `business_metrics` exports your real cost per task. |
| **Entire** | Checkpoints are stored in git refs, and you have 1 Claude Code checkpoint out of 48 commits. |

## Fix these before you record

1. **The Entire overview's headline is "Stop capturing Claude Code sessions with Entire."** Ashish's latest commit (`f4580ee`) removed the Entire hooks. Two of the five judges are from Entire, and that's the first thing they'll see. Turn capture back on for one real fix session (the commit used `entire agent remove claude-code`, so `entire agent add claude-code` is probably the reverse). The commit from that session then becomes the headline, with a checkpoint attached.
2. **There's no Neatlogs before/after yet, and this is the biggest scoring gap.** Your Neatlogs dashboard already gives you the "before": 13.7% errors. The cause is real. In [safe_fetch.py:167](../AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/integrations/safe_fetch.py:167), `fetch_webpage` sends `Accept-Encoding: identity`, but some sites send gzip anyway, and the agent then throws the page away. The same check exists in the Exa and Tavily clients. The loop to run:
   - Run 5 fixed prompts with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=baseline`.
   - In Claude Code, with the Neatlogs MCP and Entire both on, ask it to find the cause from the trace.
   - Fix it with bounded gzip/deflate decompression (cap the decompressed size).
   - Re-run the same 5 prompts with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=improved` and record the numbers.

   That one session gives you footage for both Neatlogs and Entire.
3. **Neatlogs shows "traces stopped flowing."** Make sure the worker you record with has `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` set. Set `NEATLOGS_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true` only for the demo task (it shows inputs and responses), and check that trace for secrets before you show it.
4. **Neatlogs spend shows $0.00006.** That's because it doesn't have a price for `gpt-6-luna`. Don't linger on that tile; your ledger is the real cost figure.
5. **The cfo.ai model doesn't exist yet.** Connect CFO.ai on AgentForge's Plugins page, give the agent the `business_metrics` JSON, and have it build the pricing and runway model. Then the agent planned its own business.
6. **Building in public is 15%.** Post on X with #neatHack today: the Neatlogs error screenshot, the fix, and the before/after numbers.

## The story

**"Trust needs three things: it can't break anything, you approve what matters, and you can see every step afterwards."** That's the hackathon's own tagline turned into your product. Neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai then come in as the way you *built, improved and planned* AgentForge, which is the wording of the 25% criterion.

## Demo script (target 2:50; the limit is 3:00)

Values in `[brackets]` are numbers you'll measure. Don't record until they're real.

**0:00–0:15: Hook**
*Screen:* the landing page at agentforge.vexelityai.com, then a new chat.
> "neatHack asked for agents you'd trust to run without watching. Trust takes three things: the agent can't break anything, you approve what matters, and you can see every step after. That's AgentForge."

**0:15–1:10: The agent (30%)**
*Screen:* a small public repo with a real bug and a failing test. Select the repo, choose **Ask me**, and type: *"Issue #1: [bug]. Find the cause, fix it, prove it with tests, open a draft PR."*
Then show, in order:
- the sub-agent cards ("3 subagents · 2 working")
- the sandbox `bash` test run failing
- the approval card showing the exact edit, then click Approve
- the tests passing
- the PR approval card listing the changed files
- the draft PR on GitHub

Put a "sped up 4×" label on screen.
> "I give it a real issue on a real repo, in Ask me mode. It reads the code at a pinned commit, then splits the work: three sub-agents investigate in parallel, each with its own card and report. It runs the tests in its own E2B sandbox, which holds no secrets. They fail. It finds the cause, and before changing a single file it stops and shows me the exact edit. I approve. Tests pass. Then the pull request: every changed file is listed before it opens, and our backend opens it, so GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox. Plan, tools, failure, fix, verification, delivery. Start to finish."

**1:10–1:55: Neatlogs**
*Screen:*
- The hero task's trace: the span tree, then `tool_approval` (guardrail) and `delegate_task` with the sub-agent nested under it.
- Neatlogs home showing **13.7%** errors.
- The failure trace: `fetch_webpage` ERROR, and the root span COMPLETED with `tool_failures=2`.
- Claude Code with the Neatlogs MCP pointing at `safe_fetch.py`.
- The baseline and improved runs side by side.

> "Every run is a Neatlogs trace, and every conversation is a session: model calls with tokens, each tool call, sub-agents nested under their parent, and my approvals as guardrail spans. Only metadata leaves our worker by default. Neatlogs showed a 13.7% error rate. code analysis.

Export internal cost aggregates with:

```sh
cd apps/api
uv run python -m agentforge.operations.business_metrics --days 7 --output /secure-path/agentforge-costs.json
```

This performs SELECT-only aggregation across application users and creates a new
mode-0600 file. It exports task counts and measured/conservative ledger costs;
unknown operation costs retain their recorded upper bound. No goals, prompts,
user/task IDs, repository names, artifact content or secrets are included. It is
operator-only business evidence, **not** a provider invoice or cfo.ai export.

|---|---|

content.text:
I did what I could from here. Nothing is committed or pushed. The most useful result: your own data gives a better Neatlogs story than the one in my first script.

## What your real data shows

From your Neatlogs project (via its API) and your local database (read-only queries):

| Finding | Number |
|---|---|
| `fetch_webpage` calls that failed | **22 of 39 (56%)**: 13 `FETCH_HTTP_ERROR`, 5 `SCOPE_DENIED`, 3 `FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED`, 1 too large |
| Times the agent retried the **exact same failing URL** in one task | **4, and all 4 failed again**, in 3 tasks |
| Example hosted trace `6714884f…` | fetch ERROR after 162 ms; 4 model calls, **29,947 tokens in, 198 out** |
| Token mix over 7 days | **1.54M input vs 16k output**: about 99% of tokens are context |

I tested why the fetches fail:
- **Bot walls.** npm, Stack Overflow, Medium, G2 and Indeed return 403 even to a normal browser user-agent. Changing headers won't fix that, and you shouldn't try to get around it.
- **The real agent bug is how it recovers.** It retries a URL that just failed instead of using the search results it already has. That fits the hackathon's "Recovery" focus area exactly.
- **Compression is the second, smaller fix.** Some servers send gzip even when the agent asks for uncompressed pages.

## What I changed in `C:\Coding\AgentForge`

1. **Re-installed the Entire hooks for Claude Code** (`entire agent add claude-code`). This changes `.claude/settings.json` and undoes Ashish's commit `f4580ee`. Check with Ashish before pushing, in case he removed them for privacy.
2. **Added `.mcp.json`** so Claude Code connects to the Neatlogs MCP. It reads the key from an environment variable, so no secret is in the file. I checked that the endpoint answers with your key: it offers 26 tools, including `search_traces`, `get_project_analytics`, `triage_*` and `create_detection`.
3. **Updated `docs/hackathon.md`.** It no longer mentions entire-graph; Entire is described as checkpoints only, and CFO.ai as a plugin.
4. **Updated `docs/neatlogs.md`.** It now says the MCP is configured and checked.

I didn't write the fix itself. If I did it from here, Entire wouldn't capture it, because this session runs in the farmleaf folder. It needs its own session in AgentForge so the checkpoint becomes your demo footage.

## What you do next

**1. Make the Neatlogs key available to Claude Code.** This copies it from `.env` without displaying it. Restart the Claude app afterwards.
```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('NEATLOGS_API_KEY', ((Get-Content C:\Coding\AgentForge\.env | Select-String '^NEATLOGS_API_KEY=').Line -replace "^NEATLOGS_API_KEY=['""]?|['""]?$",''), 'User')
```

**2. Record the baseline.** Start the local worker with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=baseline`. Run each of these prompts in a new conversation:
1. `Open https://www.npmjs.com/package/react and tell me the latest version and weekly downloads.`
2. `Summarise the top answer at https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38987 in 3 bullets.`
3. `Read https://openai.com/api/pricing/ and list the per-million-token prices.`
4. `Fetch https://www.g2.com/products/linear/reviews and summarise what reviewers complain about.`
5. `Summarise https://docs.astral.sh/uv/ in 5 bullets.` (a control that should pass)

**3. Open a new Claude Code session in `C:\Coding\AgentForge`** and paste this prompt:

> Use the neatlogs MCP. Search the traces tagged `baseline` in workflow `agentforge-ai` and get project analytics for `fetch_webpage` failures. Then fix what they show:
> 1. **The agent repeats failed calls.** In `apps/api/src/agentforge/tools/gateway.py`, if a call in the same task has the same tool and args digest as one that already failed with a non-transient code, don't run it again. Non-transient means: `FETCH_HTTP_ERROR` for 4xx only (check how it separates 4xx from 5xx/429), `FETCH_COMPRESSED_CONTENT_REJECTED`, `SCOPE_DENIED`, `FETCH_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE`. Return the original code with a short note: it already failed, so use another source, such as the search result content through `read_research_source`. Keep it as an ERROR tool span so Neatlogs shows it.
> 2. **Compressed pages.** In `apps/api/src/agentforge/integrations/safe_fetch.py:167`, decode gzip/deflate with a decompressed-size cap equal to `max_bytes`, so it's safe against zip bombs. Keep rejecting other encodings. Do the same in `exa_client.py` and `tavily_client.py`.
> 3. Use `create_detection` to add a Neatlogs detection for "same tool, same arguments, failed twice in one trace", if the tool supports it.
>
> Add tests, run them, and make one commit.

**4. Record the improved run.** Restart the worker with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=improved` and run the same 5 prompts. Compare failed fetches, repeated calls, tokens and duration per trace. Those are the before/after numbers for the video.

## Updated Neatlogs voiceover (replaces my first version)

> "Neatlogs showed us more than half our page fetches failed: 22 of 39. Worse, the agent kept retrying a URL that had already failed, and every retry failed again. Claude Code read those traces through the Neatlogs MCP, found the cause in our tool gateway, and fixed how the agent recovers. Same five tasks, before and after: failed fetches went from [X] to [Y], and tokens per task from [A] to [B]. And we turned the bug into a Neatlogs detection, so it can't come back quietly."

## Inputs for cfo.ai

These come from 18 local tasks, so label them as a small sample:
- Conservative cost per **successful** task (includes failed attempts): **$0.10**
- Median task: **$0.011**
- 95th percentile task: **$0.157**

The export also counts 9 of the 18 tasks as partial, an older status, and none failed. The JSON is in my scratchpad as `agentforge-costs-local.json`.

Your hosted server will have more data: run `business_metrics` there. On your local machine, the full export command fails until you run `alembic upgrade head`, because your local database is at migration `0019`. I didn't migrate it.

Prompt to give AgentForge, with the CFO.ai plugin connected:
> "Here's our measured cost per task: [paste JSON]. Build a model in CFO.ai with a Free tier and a Pro tier, base and downside scenarios, gross margin and 12-month runway. Label every assumption."

Here's the order to do things in. Submissions open at 7:00 PM IST tonight and are planned to close at 11:55 PM.

## Step by step

**1. Post on X now (5 min).** Building in public is 15% of the score, and a post made before you've fixed anything is worth the most. Screenshot the Neatlogs dashboard showing the 13.7% error rate and post something like:
> "Building AgentForge for #neatHack. @neatlogs just showed us 56% of our agent's page fetches fail, and it keeps retrying URLs that already failed. Fixing it today, before/after numbers coming."

**2. Set the Neatlogs key for Claude Code, then restart the Claude app (2 min).** Run the PowerShell command from my last message, then fully quit and reopen Claude.

**3. Run the baseline (20 min).**
- Start the local stack with `NEATLOGS_TAGS=baseline` set in `.env`, then run `scripts/dev.sh`.
- Run the 5 baseline prompts, one new conversation each.
- Screenshot the Neatlogs traces with the failing `fetch_webpage` spans.

**4. Do the fix in a new Claude Code session (45 min).**
- Open a new session with the folder set to `C:\Coding\AgentForge`.
- Before you start, check that Entire is watching: run `entire status` and confirm the hooks are installed.
- Paste the fix prompt from my last message.
- **Screen-record this session.** It's your Neatlogs-MCP and Entire footage.
- Let it commit.

**5. Run the improved version (20 min).** Change `.env` to `NEATLOGS_TAGS=improved`, restart `scripts/dev.sh`, and run the same 5 prompts. Write down the before/after numbers: failed fetches, repeated calls, tokens and duration. **Post #2 on X** with those numbers.

**6. Push (10 min).**
- Agree with Ashish about turning the Claude Code hooks back on.
- Commit my changes as their own commit: `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json` and the two docs.
- Push both commits.
- Open the Entire page and check that the fix commit shows a checkpoint (the orange Claude Code marker).

**7. Build the cfo.ai model (30 min).**
- Connect CFO.ai on AgentForge's Plugins page.
- Give the agent the cost numbers and the prompt from my last message.
- Screenshot the model in cfo.ai: pricing, margin and runway.
- **Post #3 on X.**

**8. Record the hero task (30 min).** Use a small repo with a real bug and Ask me mode, and capture these on screen:
- the sub-agent cards
- the failing test
- the approval card, then Approve
- the passing test
- the draft PR

If you record on agentforge.vexelityai.com, deploy the fix and run `alembic upgrade head` there first. Otherwise record locally.

**9. Edit the video (60 min).** Follow the script, filling in your real numbers, and keep it under 3:00. Check every frame for keys and `.env` values. Upload it publicly, as unlisted YouTube or Loom.

**10. Submit (after 7:00 PM).** Quote-post the official neatlogs post with your team name, project, public repo link and video link. Save the URL of your post.

## If you're short on time

Cut in this order:
1. Leave the `create_detection` part out of the fix prompt.
2. Leave out the compression fix and keep only the repeated-call fix.
3. Do the cfo.ai model by hand in cfo.ai instead of through the plugin.

Never cut the before/after numbers or the Entire checkpoint. Four of the five judges are from Neatlogs or Entire.

Start with steps 1 and 2. Once the baseline traces are in, send me screenshots and I'll check them before you do the fix.

content.text:
It isn't set yet. Here's what it's for and how to do it.

## What it's for

The `.mcp.json` I pushed tells Claude Code: "connect to the Neatlogs MCP server and log in with `${NEATLOGS_API_KEY}`." That gives Claude Code tools to read your Neatlogs traces directly, like `search_traces` and `get_trace_context`. In the fix session you can then just ask: "look at my failing traces and find the cause."

The key isn't written in `.mcp.json`, because that file is on GitHub and would leak it. Claude Code reads it from a Windows environment variable called `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`. Right now that variable doesn't exist, so the Neatlogs connection would fail to log in.

## How to set it (2 minutes)

**1.** Open PowerShell, the normal Windows one. Run this, as a single line:
```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('NEATLOGS_API_KEY', ((Get-Content C:\Coding\AgentForge\.env | Select-String '^NEATLOGS_API_KEY=').Line -replace "^NEATLOGS_API_KEY=['""]?|['""]?$",''), 'User')
```
It copies the key from your AgentForge `.env` into a Windows user variable. It doesn't print the key anywhere.

**2. Fully quit the Claude app.** Closing the window isn't enough: right-click the Claude icon in the taskbar tray and choose Quit. Then open it again. Programs only pick up new environment variables when they start.

**3. Start a new Claude Code session with the folder set to `C:\Coding\AgentForge`.** The connection only exists in that folder, because `.mcp.json` lives there.

**4. Check it works.** In that new session:
- If Claude Code asks whether to trust or enable the `neatlogs` MCP server from `.mcp.json`, choose **Allow**.
- Type: `Use the neatlogs MCP whoami tool.` It should answer with your Neatlogs project. If it does, you're connected.

## If it doesn't connect

- **It says unauthorized, or `whoami` fails:** the app didn't pick up the variable. Make sure you fully quit it, not just closed the window.
- **The neatlogs server isn't listed at all:** the session isn't opened in `C:\Coding\AgentForge`.
- If it still fails, tell me what it says and I'll check the variable from here.

Once `whoami` works, you're ready for the baseline runs and then the fix session.

DATABASE_URL=<set>
LOCAL_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN=<set>
LLM_MODEL=<set>
LLM_API_KEY=<set>
LLM_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=<set>
LLM_SUPPORTS_JSON=<set>
LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS=<set>
LLM_INPUT_USD_PER_MILLION=<set>

---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the API, the worker and the web app together with prefixed output. Ctrl-C stops all three.
# Usage: scripts/dev.sh
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
if command -v corepack >/dev/null 2>&1; then PNPM="corepack pnpm"; else PNPM="pnpm"; fi
pids=()

# Each process gets its own process group, so stopping it also stops whatever it spawned (uvicorn reloader, next).
start() {
  local name="$1" directory="$2"; shift 2
  set -m
  ( cd "$ROOT/$directory" && "$@" 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do printf '[%s] %s\n' "$name" "$line"; done ) &
  pids+=("$!")
  set +m
}

stop() {
  trap - INT TERM EXIT
  echo "Stopping..."
  for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do kill -TERM -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done
  wait 2>/dev/null
  exit "${1:-0}"
}
trap stop INT TERM EXIT

start api    apps/api uv run uvicorn agentforge.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload --no-access-log
start worker apps/api uv run python -m agentforge.workers.runner
start web    apps/web $PNPM dev

# Stop everything as soon as any one of them exits, so a crash is not hidden behind the others' output.
while :; do
  for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do
    if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "A process exited; stopping the others."
      stop 1
    fi
  done
  sleep 1
done

from agentforge.settings import get_settings

for o in out: print(json.dumps(o))
tot = {k: sum(o[k] for o in out) for k in ("seconds","tool_calls","failed","repeated_after_fail","model_calls","input_tokens","output_tokens","cost_usd")}

| # | Prompt | Time | Tool calls | Failed or blocked | Tokens | Neatlogs trace |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| **Total** | | **7.9 min** | **95** | **16** | **1.08M in / 18k out** | ledger cost **$0.12** |

## What the traces show

1. **The biggest problem: in every one of the 5 tasks, the agent's first step was blocked.** It isn't allowed to open the link the user pasted. `fetch_webpage` only accepts URLs that came back from a web search ([policies.py:176](../AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/security/policies.py:176)). So every task fails with `SCOPE_DENIED`, searches, and only then fetches. The web app sends the same empty host list ([conversation-composer.tsx:154](../AgentForge/apps/web/features/sessions/conversation-composer.tsx:154)), so real users hit this too. It isn't caused by my test driver.
2. **64% of page fetches failed or were blocked** (16 of 25). The failures that aren't blocks are mostly sites returning 403 to bots.
3. **Task 3 got stuck in a search loop.** After the OpenAI page was blocked, it ran 37 web searches: 206 seconds and 430k tokens for one pricing question.
4. **98% of tokens are input**, meaning context, and 4 of the 5 traces show as `error` in Neatlogs.
5. **Compression failures: zero in this run.** I've dropped that from the fix so the story stays honest.

## The fix to make next (in a new Claude Code session in `C:\Coding\AgentForge`)

Paste this prompt:
